source.title: To Each Optimizer a Norm, To Each Norm its Generalization
source.authors: Sharan Vaswani; Reza Babanezhad; J. Gallego; Aaron Mishkin; Simon Lacoste-Julien; Nicolas Le Roux

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports optimizer and generalization results in synthetic linear regression and classification settings, extending optimizer comparisons beyond the image and language benchmarks named in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites prior optimizer comparisons and reports many theory and training-loss results; cited results and training-loss-only results are not catalog rows. Figure-only values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study compares adaptive and nonadaptive optimizers' held-out performance in linear and NTK regression and synthetic classification, extending V4 to new settings. Its projection experiments also address a separate claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. More precisely, interpolating regression solutions minimize corresponding quadratic norms, while separating classifiers have directions corresponding to maximum-margin solutions in suitable quadratic norms. Projections and switching can improve generalization, and classification requires attention to data geometry. Extension to deep nonlinear networks remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic linear and NTK experiments rather than the image-classification and language benchmarks in V4; optimizer and data-span projection interventions are studied.
record.method_sensitivity: Adagrad's test performance depends strongly on step size; projection onto the data span and switching to GD affect test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Data-span projection improves synthetic classification test accuracy; the one-time projection and switching variant raises accuracy from 64% to 66%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restricting optimizer solutions to the training-data span can improve generalization in overparameterized linear classification.

fits_no_version.finding: Covariance-based preconditioning improves classification alignment with the Bayes classifier, while natural-gradient preconditioning gives the worst generalization among the tested regression methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization benefit of a quadratic norm or preconditioner depends on the task and data geometry.

record.problems: The generalization experiments are synthetic linear or NTK-based; several comparisons are described qualitatively or presented only in figures. The paper states that test performance is evaluated on sampled test examples for NTK experiments, and repeats synthetic regression experiments ten times with median and inter-quartile range.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only regression curves in Figures 2, 4, and 5 are not individually transcribed because exact plotted values are unavailable in the text. Figure 9 projection comparisons and additional classification plots are not separate rows where the text gives no distinct measured test-performance outcome.

untested.parts: No comparison of fixed random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
No width sweep establishing continued test-error improvement beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.

Image and language benchmarks, learning-rate decay schedules, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and word-level language-model exceptions are untested. The switching experiment uses Adagrad and GD.
The deterministic-gradient ablation does not establish a batch-size penalty under matched epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization gaps.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence.

missing.what: Full-matrix Adagrad and GD converge to the same minimum-norm regression solution, whereas diagonal Adagrad does not; record the corresponding generalization comparison for batch and minibatch gradients.
missing.locator: Section 2.1; Appendix E.1.2, Figure 7; Appendix E.2.4

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly describes all generalization experiments as synthetic: Appendix E.1.1 also evaluates wine and mushroom data using NTK regression. Results explicitly declared in rows_left_out are not repeated as missing. No exact values were reconstructed from the extracted figure layouts.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not compared.
The paper varies hidden width for regression experiments, but does not test whether classification test error keeps falling beyond the interpolation threshold.

Tests synthetic linear regression and classification only; does not test image-classification or language benchmarks, limited-tuning schedules, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or the word-level language-model exception.
A batch-gradient ablation is reported, but the study does not test the large-batch penalty under fixed epoch budgets described by this version.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- and margin-based generalization measures.

rows.subject: Adagrad
rows.size_stated: NTK features from one-layer networks with 50 and 100 hidden units
rows.operation_detail: Trained with squared loss on synthetic over-parameterized regression; compared step sizes.

conditions.value: synthetic regression using one-layer-network NTK features

rows.value: Test performance depends strongly on step size; no exact test-loss values stated in text.
rows.note: Authors state that Adagrad test performance highly depends on step size; the figure's exact values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Step-size sensitivity alone does not establish worse generalization than SGD. Read with R2 and Appendix E.1.1, the results show a step-size-dependent disadvantage, rather than uniformly poor Adagrad performance.

rows.subject: SGD
rows.size_stated: NTK features from one-layer networks with 50 and 100 hidden units
rows.operation_detail: Trained with squared loss on synthetic over-parameterized regression using hand-tuned step size.

conditions.value: synthetic regression using one-layer-network NTK features

rows.value: Authors state the min-norm solution found by SGD consistently generalizes well.
rows.note: The text characterizes SGD as generalizing well but supplies no exact test-loss value here.
rows.check: This is a comparator row: SGD generalizing well alone cannot establish an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage. The relevant comparison is with R1. The NTK experiment details and tuning grid are in Appendix E.2.2.

rows.subject: Adagrad
rows.operation_detail: Trained on synthetic over-parameterized linear classification, then switched to GD after 75% of iterations.

conditions.value: synthetic classification with random Gaussian features

rows.baseline: standard Adagrad; exact value not stated
rows.value: switching to GD results in a small improvement; exact value not stated
rows.note: The authors describe the improvement as small.
rows.check: The reported improvement from switching is small. Figure 3 uses 1000 random Gaussian features, not networks with 50 and 100 hidden units. The intervention switches Adagrad to full-batch GD, rather than Adam to SGD.

rows.subject: Adagrad
rows.operation_detail: Projected the final solution onto the data span and switched to GD after 75% of iterations.

conditions.value: synthetic over-parameterized classification with random Gaussian features

rows.note: The text explicitly states the before and after accuracies for projecting only the final solution.
rows.check: The 64% to 66% comparison concerns data-span projection combined with switching; it does not isolate the switching effect in V4. The one-time projection occurs at the switch point, before subsequent GD iterations, rather than after all optimization.

rows.subject: Adagrad
rows.operation_detail: Projected the final solution onto the data span and switched from Adagrad to GD at the switch point.

conditions.value: 75% of iterations in the plotted setting

rows.note: Text says projection improves test accuracy; plotted values are not stated numerically. Results aggregated over 10 data samples.
rows.check: Projection benefits do not directly test V4. This row combines multiple feature counts, learning rates, and projection variants. One-time projection occurs at the switch point; the appendix also evaluates projection after every iteration.

relationships.condition: Unprojected diagonal Adagrad at unfavorable step sizes in overparameterized NTK regression
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 show step-size-dependent Adagrad generalization versus consistently good SGD generalization; Appendix E.1.1 explicitly describes poor Adagrad generalization despite fast training convergence.
relationships.display_finding: The reported poor Adagrad generalization despite fast training convergence remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Switching Adagrad to GD late in synthetic overparameterized logistic classification
relationships.reason: R3 reports only a small test-accuracy improvement from switching, so recovery is modest in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: The reported small test-accuracy improvement from switching Adagrad to GD remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Full-matrix Adagrad on well-conditioned synthetic linear regression
relationships.reason: Based on text, with a missing row: Appendix E.1.2 and Figure 7 report convergence to the same minimum-norm solution as GD, giving equal limiting generalization for this adaptive variant.
relationships.display_finding: Reported convergence to GD's minimum-norm solution and equal limiting generalization remains unverified.
